response.text:
Free, Open-source Anonymous Email Forwarding - addy.io

# A different email address for every website 

addy.io creates aliases that forward to your real inbox. Share an alias instead of your main email address - then switch one off if it leaks or starts spamming you. 

 

### 1. Choose a username

Pick a username (for example johndoe). You can then use an email address like anything@johndoe.addy.io - the bit before the @ sign can be whatever you like.

Want to stay anonymous? Pick a username that is not tied to your real name and that you have not used elsewhere online.

You can also use shared domains (e.g. @addy.io) so your addresses do not all contain the same username.

### 2. Give each site its own email

When you sign up somewhere, invent a new alias instead of typing your real email address. You can think one up on the spot or generate one in advance - either way works.

Example: for a Groupon newsletter you might use groupon@johndoe.addy.io.

We add the alias to your dashboard when the first message arrives. You can reply and send from aliases without exposing your real email address. 

### 3. Turn off what you do not want

If an address starts getting junk mail, open your dashboard and deactivate that alias.

We then silently discard new mail to it - nothing reaches your inbox for that alias.

Delete an alias if you prefer senders to get a bounce instead of a quiet drop.

 

### Mobile apps

Beautiful mobile apps with a buttery smooth user experience to manage your account on the go. 

Completely free to use whether you are using addy.io or your own self-hosted instance.

The mobile apps are available on iOS and Android and are both open-source.

 

 

### Browser extension

Create a new alias in a couple of clicks while you browse, using our open-source extension.

Available in Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Safari, and other Chromium-based browsers such as Brave and Vivaldi.

### GPG / OpenPGP encryption

Bring your own GPG/OpenPGP public keys and add them per recipient. 

You can then easily toggle encryption on and off. With encryption on, all forwarded messages will be encrypted with your public key. Only you will be able to decrypt them with the corresponding private key. You can even hide and encrypt the email subject!

This is great if you are using Gmail or Outlook and wish to prevent any inbox snooping.

 

### Your own domain

Bring a domain you control and create addresses like anything@example.com, the same way you do with your username subdomain.

You can also enable or disable the catch-all functionality for each of your domains.

Prefer not to use catch-all? You can still create aliases on the fly with a regular expression match.

If an address starts attracting spam, deactivate or delete it from your dashboard.

### Random aliases

Don't want your username in every address? Generate one-off aliases from your dashboard.

They look like x481n904@anonaddy.me or weekly-warning694@addy.io - harder for anyone to tie back to you.

Useful when you want separation without a recognisable pattern.

 

### Reply and send from aliases 

Reply anonymously to forwarded emails, the sender will receive the email as if it has come from the alias.

You can even initiate an email conversation by sending an email from one of your aliases.

Your real email address is not revealed when replying or sending from an alias.

### Add additional usernames

Add more usernames to the same account and use them like your first one.

Example: if you signed up as johndoe, add johnsmith and you can use anything@johnsmith.addy.io as well.

Handy for separating work, personal, or any other life area without juggling multiple accounts.

### Multiple recipients per alias 

Route one alias to multiple real email addresses from your dashboard.

You can send bills or service alerts to you and your partner, forward support emails to a team inbox, or keep a backup address so important messages are still delivered if one mailbox is unavailable.

For example, waterbills@yourdomain.com can forward to both your personal inbox and your partner's inbox at the same time.

### Developer API

Automate aliases, recipients, domains, additional usernames and other account resources with the addy.io API.

Create an API key in your account settings to get started.
